title: Edit confidently with vi
goal: Use modes, navigation, search and editing to create a precise file change.
challenge: In vi change Beta to Beta revised, duplicate that line and remove Gamma, leaving Alpha and two Beta revised lines. Preserve the original; explain insertion, normal and command-line modes, search and save.

steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace. Stop if creation or cd fails. Retain its printed path; variables do not survive disk Resume.
steps.expected: A fresh directory inside the guest home; no existing files are changed.

steps.command: printf '%s\n' Alpha Beta Gamma > note.txt; cp -p note.txt original.txt
steps.explanation: Make a backup before entering the actual guest vi implementation.
Inside vi: Escape, 1G, j, 0, cw; type Beta revised; Escape; yy; p; /Gamma then Enter; dd; :wq then Enter. Commands in normal mode are not shell commands. h/j/k/l navigate.
steps.expected: Saved file: Alpha then Beta revised twice. Original remains unchanged.

steps.command: cat note.txt; diff -u original.txt note.txt; command -v vi; vi --version | head -2
steps.explanation: Review the result and actual implementation. The pinned image routes vi to vim.tiny; this is not every feature of full Vim.
steps.expected: Intended three-line edit and implementation information.

hints: What changes when Escape leaves insertion mode?
Compare actual output, immediate exit status and resulting files. A syntactically valid command or script can still do the wrong thing.
Keep the original, verify a small intended change, and demonstrate rollback inside this workspace.
review: I retained the stated observations and can explain the outcome.
I checked failure cases and preserved originals; my review is not an application-verified score.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 103.8. Reinforcement is labeled; no full-objective mastery. Completion records self-review, not verified assessment. No score.
